title: .github/agents/doc-updater.agent.md (Copilot harness) is missing the project-board-update step present in .claude/agents/doc-updater.md
summary: While fixing ISS-XXXX (DOC-UPDATER never closes a requirement's own GitHub tracking issue at Step Final), found that .github/agents/doc-updater.agent.md's GitHub Branch Management section is a full independent copy of .claude/agents/doc-updater.md's, not a pointer -- and it is missing an entire step present in the canonical file: step 5, updating the GitHub Project board per docs/agents/protocols/PROJECT_BOARD.md (python tools/gh_project_status.py ... --target implemented/done for issues this run resolves). The Copilot-harness DOC-UPDATER therefore never updates the project board at all, only the Claude-harness one does. This is pre-existing drift, not something introduced by the requirement-tracking-issue fix -- confirmed by grep: 'gh_project_status' and 'PROJECT_BOARD' appear zero times in .github/agents/doc-updater.agent.md.

root_cause.details: Per CLAUDE.md's 'Canonical instruction surfaces' section: '.github/agents/*.md and .github/instructions/*.md are the parallel entry point for the GitHub Copilot harness; they are adapters, not a second canonical copy -- if one of them disagrees with its .claude/agents/ counterpart, that is a defect to report, not two valid variants to keep in sync by hand.' The two files were evidently maintained independently at some point (the Copilot mirror is a full rewrite, not a thin adapter/pointer), and PROJECT_BOARD.md's step was added to the canonical .claude/agents/doc-updater.md without the corresponding update ever being made to the Copilot mirror.

prevention: Add the missing project-board-update step to .github/agents/doc-updater.agent.md, mirroring .claude/agents/doc-updater.md's step 5 exactly.

Consider whether the .github/agents/*.md files should become thin pointers into .claude/agents/*.md rather than full independent copies, to make this class of drift structurally impossible rather than relying on manual sync discipline.
A periodic or CI-driven diff check between the two harness's agent instruction sets (excluding harness-specific frontmatter) would catch this class of drift automatically.
